itens.titulo: Tesla profits drop but top analyst estimates
itens.descricao: Tesla profits drop but top analyst estimates Yahoo Finance
trechos: Tesla reported a drop in third-quarter profits Wednesday but topped analyst estimates as multi-billionaire Elon Musk's electric vehicle maker invested heavily in new technologies.
Texas-based Tesla reported profits of $787 million, down 42.7 percent from the year-ago period.
Revenues were essentially flat at $28 billion.

"We continue to invest in the future through R&D and Capex spend across our businesses, including SI, robotics and energy," said Tesla, referring to the Trump administration's favored term, "Super Intelligence" instead of artificial intelligence.
"Much hard work lies ahead, but we are as optimistic as ever," the company added in the earnings release.
Also impactful, capital spending more than doubled to $4.7 billion.
Musk has repeatedly made overly rosy forecasts about self-driving technology, as in 2019 when predicted there would be more than a million robotaxis the following year.
In Texas, where Tesla has focused its robotaxi launch, there are currently about 800 robotaxis, according to FSD Database.

itens.titulo: Treasury yields steady as investors await jobless claims
itens.descricao: Treasury yields steady as investors await jobless claims CNBC
trechos: Treasury — the main benchmark for mortgages, auto loans and credit card debt — was up less than 1 basis point at 5.123%.
The yield on the 2-year Treasury note, which more closely follows short-term Federal Reserve rate decisions, rose more than 2 basis points to 4.808%.
The yield on longer-dated 30-year U.S.
Treasurys — which often moves on geopolitical developments — moved more than 1 basis point lower to 5.411%.
One basis point equals 0.01%, or 1/100th of 1%, and yields and prices move inversely to one another.
28, traders are weighing up how domestic economic data and global geopolitical developments are shaping the outlook for inflation and interest rates.
The average 30-year fixed-rate mortgage declined to 7.41% last week, according to the Mortgage Bankers Association.
The fixed-rate loan average was previously at 7.5%.
